newsitem.title: UK: P&O shares jump on channel ferry merger.
newsitem.headline: P&O shares jump on channel ferry merger.

text.p: P&O shares leapt to their highest level in more than a year in early trading on Thursday after the company said it would merge its short-sea ferry businesses on the English Channel with those of rival Stena Line AB of Sweden. The stock was up 16-1/2p at 641-1/2 by 0714 GMT, its highest since June 1995.
Responding to increased competition from Eurotunnel Plc, the two companies said they expected to be able to cut costs by 75 million stg from a fixed cost base of some 280 million stg.

Analysts said the deal was seen as another positive move as chairman Lord Sterling tackles the group's underperforming businesses with renewed vigour, though the problem of competition from Eurotunnel remained.

"It is being viewed as a very positive deal and the pace at which Sterling is moving is quite remarkable," said one analyst. "Shareholders are clearly enjoying the ride but the point we would also make is that it is still a very tough market."
"It is a defensive rather than offensive move and Eurotunnel is still a potent force."
Last month P&O said it planned to merge its container shipping business with Nedlloyd NV of the Netherlands.
Today's merger was foreshadowed in comments by Stena's managing director Bo Lerenius on September 9 that he wanted to work with the UK company.
